questions.stem: Which three factors mainly affect the rate of photosynthesis?

options.text: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature

questions.explanation: The three main factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis are light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature.

questions.stem: How does increasing light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis?

options.text: It increases the rate up to a point, then the rate levels off
It only affects the rate at night

questions.explanation: Increasing light intensity increases the rate of photosynthesis up to a point, after which the rate levels off because another factor (such as CO2 concentration or temperature) becomes limiting.

questions.stem: What is the inverse square law in relation to light intensity?

options.text: Light intensity doubles when distance doubles
Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the light source
Light has no relationship with distance
Light intensity stays constant at all distances

questions.explanation: The inverse square law states that light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source. If distance doubles, light intensity decreases to one quarter.

questions.stem: Why does the rate of photosynthesis decrease at very high temperatures?

options.text: Enzymes involved in photosynthesis become denatured

questions.explanation: At very high temperatures, the enzymes that catalyse the reactions of photosynthesis become denatured - their active sites change shape and they can no longer function.

questions.stem: How can you measure the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed?

options.text: By counting bubbles of oxygen produced per minute or collecting gas in a syringe
By measuring the temperature of the water
By measuring the growth of the plant

questions.explanation: The rate of photosynthesis in pondweed can be measured by counting oxygen bubbles per minute or by collecting the gas produced in a gas syringe over a set time period.

questions.stem: What is the typical optimum temperature for photosynthesis in most plants?
questions.explanation: Most plants have an optimum temperature for photosynthesis between 25-35 degrees C. Below this, reactions are slower; above this, enzymes begin to denature.

questions.stem: If increasing carbon dioxide concentration no longer increases the rate of photosynthesis, what has become the limiting factor?
questions.explanation: When increasing CO2 no longer increases the rate, another factor such as light intensity or temperature has become the limiting factor, restricting the maximum rate of photosynthesis.
